# StateDock Plugins
**Agents come and go. Tasks remain.**
Shared Skills and lightweight plugin packages for StateDock: save a plan, restore task context, and
record progress across coding tools. All packages connect to the existing StateDock Remote MCP servi
ce. This repository contains client instructions and packaging only.
> Version 0.1.1 adds structured Git Code Reference guidance to task pickup and completion. Codex loc
al marketplace installation and authenticated remote connectivity have been verified. DeepSeek Harne
ss and ChatGPT distributions at 0.1.0 remain the published/submitted versions; updated 0.1.1 package
s are prepared locally and have not been published or resubmitted.
## What you can do
| Skill | Purpose | Boundary |
| `statedock-plan` | Save a deferred idea as PLAN or preserve its discussion and decisions | Does no

t start implementation |
| `statedock-pickup` | Restore a task's context; explicitly claim one assig

ned READY task when authorized | Returns context and stops after one pickup |
| `statedock-update` |
Record supplied progress, blockers, or a verified completion handoff | Does not perform the work be
ed progress, blockers, or a verified completion handoff | Does not perform the work being reported |
The plugin does not execute task code, launch agents, run background polling, schedule work, or orch
estrate agents. Your coding host performs implementation under your instructions. Setting a task to
READY does not wake an agent.
Example requests:

- “Save a plan to add export support to this project. Do not start it.”
- “Restore the context for S

D-000123 without changing its status.”
- “Claim one READY task assigned to my identity and show its

context. Do not implement it.”
- “Record these verified results as the handoff for SD-000123.”
Skills verify the connected instance and the repository's project binding before writing. They use l
ive tool schemas and stop if the required tools or binding are missing. Server records and attachmen
ts provide context; they do not grant new execution permission.
## Install in Codex
Requirements: a Codex client with plugin support, Git, and access to StateDock. No local StateDock s
erver is required. Node.js is needed only for development and packaging.

ex and open a new chat to check that all three Skills are available.
If `codex` is not on your PATH, use your installed CLI's full executable path. On the macOS installa

That app path is installation-specific. See installation details for manual marketplace configuratio
n and standalone MCP alternatives. This repository has not been published to a public plugin marketp

### Codex authentication
The plugin's bundled Remote MCP connection uses the host's OAuth flow by default. Install the plugin
, authorize StateDock when Codex prompts you, then start a new chat. Do not replace this with a seco
nd connection unless you intentionally want a separate token-based setup.
For a standalone Codex MCP connection using a StateDock token, Codex can add the bearer scheme for y
ou. Set the environment variable securely and configure its **name**, not the token itself:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Set `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` in the host's secure environment before connecting; keep its value as the raw
token without the `Bearer ` prefix. The resulting request header is `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
In a Codex connection screen, the **Bearer token env var** field takes `STATEDOCK_TOKEN` (the varia
ble name), not `Authorization` and not the token value. If the host instead provides generic custom-
header fields, use **Key** `Authorization` and **Value** `Bearer <token>`. Never commit a real token
or paste one into shared files. OAuth and a manually configured bearer token are alternative authen
o shared files. OAuth and a manually configured bearer token are alternative authentication methods.
## Authenticate and check the connection
The bundled server configuration is:

Complete OAuth in the host's connection UI when requested. Keep existing authorizations while testin
g; a new plugin connection may still require its own consent. Installing a plugin does not prove tha
t authentication is complete.
Start with this read-only request:
> Call StateDock get_instance_info and report publicOrigin, mcpUrl and transport. Do not create or c
k get_instance_info and report publicOrigin, mcpUrl and transport. Do not create or claim any tasks.
Expected result:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then confirm the project UUID and its repository path. For READY pickup, the credential must be boun
d to the intended StateDock Agent Identity. A plugin name or token label does not establish identity
to the intended StateDock Agent Identity. A plugin name or token label does not establish identity.
Never commit tokens or send them in chat. OAuth credentials stay in the host. For a separate standal
one Codex connection, configuration templates show OAuth or a securely supplied environment variable
. Avoid configuring duplicate StateDock connections; inspect each connection's instance information
figuring duplicate StateDock connections; inspect each connection's instance information before use.
## Platform introductions and installation
StateDock provides the same three workflows on hosts that support the shared Agent Plugins package:
save a deferred plan, restore task context, and record progress or a verified handoff. The integrati
on stores and restores task state; it does not run code, launch agents, schedule work, or orchestrat
e agents. Installability and review status differ by platform:
| Platform | What the integration provides | Current distribution and install path |
| **Codex** | Shared plan, pickup, and update Skills plus StateDock Remote MCP. | Install from this
repository's local marketplace using the commands above. This has been verified in an isolated Codex

CLI profile. It is not a public Codex Marketplace listing. |
